newsitem.title: CANADA: Royal Bank sees Canada leading G-7 growth.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank sees Canada leading G-7 growth.

text.p: Canada will have the fastest growth of any nation in the Group of Seven at least through 1998, the country's largest bank said on Wednesday.
Royal Bank of Canada said in a report that growth is expected to double from 1.4 percent this year to 3 percent in 1997 and accelerate further to 3.5 percent in 1998.

The bank said Canada is now better positioned for long-term growth than any other time since the Second World War because of record low interest rates, a healthy world economy, low and stable inflation, and improved government finances.

Royal Bank chief economist John McCallum said in a statement that cuts in interest rates over the past year could create up to 315,000 new jobs by the end of 1998, and further cuts could create even more jobs.

Canada's central bank has lowered short-term interest rates by five percentage points since it began easing in May, 1995. Prime lending rate charged by banks to their best customers are now at a 40-year low of 4.75 percent.
"These lower interest rates should kick-start two levels of the economy that have been lagging -- housing and consumer spending," said McCallum.

Royal Bank noted that the central bank had lowered rates well below U.S. levels without weakening the dollar because investors were willing to buy Canadian securities yielding far less than comparable U.S. securities. That implied that investors thought the value of the Canadian dollar was going to rise, McCallum said.
